The Imperial Citadel of Thang Long, a UNESCO World Heritage site nestled in the heart of bustling Hanoi, is a testament to Vietnam's rich history and cultural heritage. Spanning an expansive area of 18,000 hectares, this ancient citadel invites visitors to immerse themselves in its storied past, offering a journey through time that begins at the entrance on 19C Hoang Dieu Street.

The archaeological exhibits within the citadel provide a detailed look at the daily life and governance of ancient Vietnam, from the construction of palaces and temples to the sophisticated drainage systems and water wells. These exhibits are complemented by temporary exhibitions such as "Hanoi - Impressions of Time," which highlights the city's evolution from 1802 to 1945, and "From the Earth to the Museum," which explores the journey of artifacts from the citadel to modern-day museums, emphasizing the shared heritage between Hanoi and Toulouse, France.
